issue_context.title: "kubectl logs --follow" has not printed new logs after log rotation.
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

When running `kubectl logs pod-name --follow`, new logs are not output to the logs command after the log file has grown and rotated.


### What did you expect to happen?

Even after log rotation, new logs are output to `kubectl logs pod-name --follow`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The following steps will reproduce it.

1. Deploy a Pod that continues to output to stdout.
2. Run `kubectl logs pod-name --follow`.
3. Wait a while and the log file will be rotated. The waiting time depends on the environment.
4. New logs will not be output to logs command.

The sample pod is following.

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pod-print
spec:
  containers:
  - name: centos7
    image: centos:7
    imagePullPolicy: Never
    command: ["sh", "-c"]
    args:
    - cnt=0;
      msg="";
      while [ $cnt -lt 5000 ];
      do
        msg="${msg} ${cnt} :loop ---------------------------";
        cnt=`expr $cnt + 1`;
      done;
      loopcnt=0;
      while true; do
        echo $msg;
        date;
        echo "loop= $loopcnt";
        loopcnt=`expr $loopcnt + 1`;
        sleep 2;
      done;
```

### Anything else we need to know?

comments:
I have investigated this issue.
I found that when the problem occurs, it always goes through the same place and then there is a problem.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/897f2f78a5c7ff659dfce23f53dd36b9261a23c9/pkg/kubelet/kuberuntime/logs/logs.go#L351-L365

When a log file is renamed by rotation, `recreated` becomes true, but immediately after the renaming, `os.Open(path)` will result in a `Not Exist` error because the new log file has not yet been created.

Then it will re-loop by continue, but since `recreated` will not be true in the next loop, it will never enter this process again.
As a result, the log after log rotation will not be read.

review_comments:
Isn't it enough to just add a retry of `os.Open(path)` if `os.IsNotExist(err)` happens?

I just want to confirm why we need to run through whole code(`r.ReadBytes()`, `f.Seek()` and `waitLogs()`) again with `continue`.
In case a log rotation happens, `r.ReadBytes()` and `f.Seek()` depend on an old file descripter and that could cause different error on each call.
I feel it would be better to just retry `os.Open()` for a new file.

@oomichi 
I thought that if a new file hasn't been created yet, there may be message still being written to the old file.
Therefore, I implemented the retry.
I have not confirmed whether such a situation actually occurs.

@s-kawamura-w664 
Sorry for my late response, and thank you so much for explaining the senario.
That is reasonable to me.

/lgtm
